label.purpose: Picker legend, meta lines, chart caption, dates, presets, callout headings.

caption.purpose: Radar Today and blip names, change chips, notice app line.

wordmark.purpose: The brand beside the radar mark; repeated huge at 9% ink in the footer.

modes.strategy: prefers-color-scheme (light and dark follow the system); '-dark' keys are the dark values of the same CSS variable
modes.highContrast: prefers-contrast: more sets --sub to ink at 80%
modes.reducedTransparency: glass, frost, chips and header become opaque --sheet with no backdrop blur
modes.forcedColors: picked chip gets a 3px Highlight outline; chart bars drawn in CanvasText, announced in Highlight

field.description: Fixed radial colour field behind every page (z-index -1), built from picked services.
field.steps: sort by monthly cost desc; skip saturation < 0.1; skip within 20deg hue of a kept spot; max 5; soften light L 0.60-0.72, dark L 0.45-0.58, S 0.45-0.80; radius = 100vw x (0.30 + 0.18 x weight / biggest)
field.quietOpacity: 0.5 past the hero (IntersectionObserver, rootMargin -30% top) and on guide, increases and privacy pages

materials.name: glass
materials.value: background: var(--glass); border: 1px solid var(--glass-border); backdrop-filter: blur(28px) saturate(1.6); box-shadow: 0 18px 50px -24px var(--shadow)
materials.purpose: Controls and live readouts: meter, pinned total, notice, Paydar card. Chips use blur(20px) saturate(1.5).

materials.name: frost
materials.value: background: var(--frost); border: 1px solid var(--frost-border); box-shadow: 0 12px 36px -22px var(--shadow)
materials.purpose: Reading content: pricing panel, cards, plan lists, charts, FAQ, increase feed.

materials.name: header
materials.value: background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--base) 85%, transparent); backdrop-filter: blur(20px) saturate(1.5); mask-image: linear-gradient(#000 calc(100% - 10px), transparent)
materials.purpose: Sticky header band that fades instead of drawing a line.

shadows.name: device
shadows.purpose: App screenshots (phone 44px corners); screen row uses 0 30px 60px -36px at 36px corners.

shadows.name: guide-logo
shadows.purpose: The 64px service logo on guide pages.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: Press feedback, blip in and out, Pro hint (--ease-out).

motion.name: press
motion.value: transform scale(.96 to .985) in 80ms, release 160ms ease-out

motion.name: hero-arrival
motion.value: rise .6s cubic-bezier(.16, 1, .3, 1), delay var(--i) x 30ms; meter .8s from translateY(24px) scale(.97) at .12s
motion.purpose: CSS-only hero entrance with the first paint; only under prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference.

motion.name: field-crossfade
motion.purpose: The field repaints when picks change.

motion.name: blip-in
motion.purpose: A new pick lands on the radar.

motion.name: blip-out
motion.purpose: A dropped pick leaves faster than it came; re-picking cancels the exit.

motion.name: count
motion.purpose: The monthly total, the pinned total and the yearly figure count to their new value.

motion.name: radar-beam
motion.value: 7s linear infinite, from 60deg; paused off-screen via IntersectionObserver

motion.name: section-entrance
motion.value: GSAP from y 28, opacity 0, .8s expo.out, stagger .08, ScrollTrigger top 82%, once
motion.purpose: Homepage sections below the hero only (heading, text, picture by data-rv); screen row drifts by scrub above 761px.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: transitions 1ms, animations none, field transition none; motion.js returns before loading Lenis or GSAP
motion.purpose: Everything instant; content visible without script.

narrative.overview:
The site is painted by the person looking at it. Paydar's 2.0 iPhone app draws its Aura from the subscriptions you track; the site does the same with the services the visitor taps. A fixed radial colour field sits behind every page, made from those services' brand colours: biggest monthly cost first, greys skipped, one colour per 20 degrees of hue, at most five spots, each softened so text stays readable, each spot's radius weighted by price, a lavender glow at the top and a veil darkening toward the bottom. Past the hero, and on every reading page, the field steps back to half strength. Light and dark follow the system; nothing is themed by hand.

Over the field, two materials and one shape do all the work. Controls and the live meter sit on glass (translucent, heavily blurred, a 1px white edge). Content that must be read sits on frost (near-opaque, the same 1px edge). Every control is a pill. Type is SF Pro at heavy weights with tight tracking, so prices and totals read as the loudest thing on the screen, with SF Pro Rounded reserved for labels, captions and the wordmark, exactly as in the app. Colour beyond the field is semantic and scarce: red means a price went up, green means good news or the way out, gold means the one-time Pro price.

Density is calm and generous: one idea per section, large type, long section gaps. The homepage is the one place with live behaviour (picker, radar, counted total, the reminder preview); guides and the price-increase feed are reading pages and stay still apart from smooth scrolling.
keyCharacteristics: A generative colour field from the visitor's own picks, fixed behind the page, quieter (0.5) past the hero and on reading pages.
Glass for controls and the meter; frost for content panels, cards and lists.
Every control a pill (999px); ink fill means primary or selected.
Heavy, tightly tracked, tabular numerals as the loudest element.
Semantic colour only: rise red, accent green, coin gold.
Real app screens and real App Store service icons, never mock imagery.

rules.name: The Visitor Paints Rule
rules.body: Saturated colour in the frame comes from the field, and the field comes from the services picked (or the page's own service), softened in light to lightness 0.60 to 0.72 and in dark to 0.45 to 0.58, saturation clamped 0.45 to 0.80. With nothing picked it falls back to green, amber and violet (#16A374, #F2B35A, #8A6BD6). Never paint a decorative gradient by hand.

rules.name: The Semantic Colour Rule
rules.body: Red appears only for price increases; green only for good news and the way out of a charge; gold only for the one-time Pro price. Brand logos and the field may carry any hue, because they are the visitor's content, not interface colour.

rules.name: The Texture Not Only Colour Rule
rules.body: Wherever red or green marks a price change in a chart, it also carries a hatch (135 degrees) and an inset outline, so the meaning never rests on hue alone.

rules.name: The Loud Numbers Rule
rules.body: A price or total is set heavier and larger than the words around it, always with tabular figures, so columns of prices align and a counted total does not jitter.

rules.name: The Rounded Is For Labels Rule
rules.body: SF Pro Rounded never sets a headline or body paragraph; it labels data and names the brand.

rules.name: The Glass For Hands, Frost For Eyes Rule
rules.body: Anything the visitor operates or watches change (chips, the meter, the pinned total, the notice, the Paydar card) is glass: blur(28px) saturate(1.6). Anything the visitor reads (pricing panel, cards, plan lists, charts, FAQ) is frost. Under Reduce Transparency both become opaque Sheet with no blur.

dos: Do derive the field from real services through the shared steps (aura.py, home.js): at most 5 spots, 20 degree hue gap, greys skipped, radius 0.30 + 0.18 times weight over the biggest weight.
Do drop the field to 0.5 opacity past the hero and on every reading page.
Do put controls and live readouts on glass and reading content on frost, with the 1px white border.
